critique: The imagery is unmistakably dandelion seed material, and t4 has a much fuller cloud than the preceding sparse result. However, the motion still reads more as accumulating seeds in a loose, broadly distributed field than a defined wind-carried release. At t1 the seeds are already dispersed across a wide central area rather than visibly originating from a compact source, and by t4 the expansion has substantial vertical and backward scatter instead of a more coherent wide rightward plume. The seeds are also very small and dim against black, reducing the thumbnail-like legibility of the botanical cloud.

suggestions.why: Shrink the emitter width so the early frame reads as a distinct seed-release source rather than seeds being born across a broad band.
Shrink the emitter height with the width to concentrate the origin and preserve a recognizable directional plume.
Narrow directional spread so the t4 cloud follows a clearer wind-driven outward/rightward trajectory instead of filling a diffuse random field.
Make individual seed sprites more visible so the wide cloud has the fuller, more legible botanical presence suggested by the preset thumbnail.
